description: Union keeps the steps of an explanation and adds the steps of another explanation whose node it does not select, in that explanation's order
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * quantity
tax = subtotal * rate
shipping = quantity * 2
(why tax |> union(why shipping)).map(step -> step.node)

description: A union begins with its own selection, so swapping the two explanations reorders the same nodes
code:
price = 10
quantity = 3
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * quantity
tax = subtotal * rate
shipping = quantity * 2
[(why shipping |> union(why tax)).map(step -> step.node), (why tax |> union(why shipping)).length]

description: A union of two impact selections lists what a change of either input reaches, each node once
code:
price = 10
rate = 0.2
subtotal = price * 3
tax = subtotal * rate
total = subtotal + tax
fee = rate * 5
(affects price |> union(affects rate)).map(step -> step.node)

description: A state filter after a union keeps the facts behind either explanation
code:
fan = 2
load = 40
speed = 3
current = load * 2
heat = current + fan
noise = fan * speed
(why heat |> union(why noise) |> stated).map(step -> step.node)

description: A depth stage after a union measures each side from where its own walk began, so a node both sides select keeps its distance in the first
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = b * 2
d = a + 3
[(why c |> union(why d) |> depth(1)).map(step -> step.node), (why c |> depth(1) |> union(why d |> depth(1))).map(step -> step.node)]

description: A walk after a union starts from every step of the union
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = b * 2
d = a + 3
f = d + 1
(b |> union(d) |> affects).map(step -> step.node)

description: A standing union follows a rule rewired on the other side
code:
a = 1
b = 2
left = a + 1
right = b + 1
either = why left |> union(why right)
c = 5
right = b + c
either.map(step -> step.node)

description: A union with model adds every other node in model order, and the union of a selection with itself is the selection
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = 4
[(why b |> union(model)).map(step -> step.node), (why b |> union(why b)).length]

description: A name that holds a selection is a reasoning observer, so it adds nothing as the other selection; the pipeline is written in place
code:
price = 10
tax = price * 2
shipping = price + 1
causes = why shipping
[(why tax |> union(causes)).length, (why tax |> union(why shipping)).length]

description: A class-level rule gives every instance its own union
code:
class Item(price, qty, fee):
    this.price = price
    this.qty = qty
    this.fee = fee
$Item.total = $Item.price * $Item.qty
$Item.cost = $Item.qty + $Item.fee
$Item.basis = why $Item.total |> union(why $Item.cost)
pen = Item(2, 5, 1)
cup = Item(3, 1, 4)
[pen.basis.map(step -> step.node), cup.basis.map(step -> step.node)]

description: Nodes names the steps of a union, and an other selection that a depth with a null limit makes undefined makes the union undefined
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
c = b * 2
d = a + 3
n = null
[c |> why |> union(d |> why) |> nodes, c |> why |> union(d |> why |> depth(n))]

description: A binding named union shadows the stage when the pipeline runs, so a try statement can catch the error
code:
a = 1
b = a + 1
union = 0
result = ""
try:
    result = why b |> union(why a)
catch error:
    result = error
[union, result]
